source.text: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις, ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν, βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων καὶ κλινῶν καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς· Διὰ τί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀλλὰ κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον;

records.literal_gloss: And are gathered together to him the Pharisees and some of the scribes having come from Jerusalem \v 2 and having seen some of the disciples of him that with defiled hands, that is, unwashed, they eat the loaves \v 3 (for the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless with [the] fist they wash the hands, not eat, holding the tradition of the elders, \v 4 and from [the] marketplace, unless they wash themselves, not eat, and other things many there are which they received to hold, washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and couches) \v 5 and question him the Pharisees and the scribes, Why not walk the disciples of you according to the tradition of the elders, but with defiled hands eat the bread?

en.L: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gather to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 2 and [they] had seen that some of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples eat [their] bread with defiled hands, that is, unwashed \v 3 (for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash [their] hands with the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders, \v 4 and [coming] from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash themselves, and there are many other things which they have received to hold to, washings of cups and pitchers and bronze vessels and couches), \v 5 and the Pharisees and the scribes question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat [their] bread with defiled hands?"
en.B: The Pharisees gathered around Jesus, together with some scribes who had come from Jerusalem. \v 2 They had noticed that some of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were eating their food with unclean hands, that is, hands not washed. \v 3 (The Pharisees, and indeed all the Jews, will not eat unless they give their hands a ritual washing, and so they keep the tradition of the elders. \v 4 When they come in from the marketplace they do not eat without first washing. They hold to many other customs that have been passed on to them as well, such as the washing of cups, pitchers, bronze pots and dining couches.) \v 5 So the Pharisees and the scribes put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples not live by the tradition of the elders? Why do they eat with unclean hands?"
en.R: Some Pharisees and some teachers of God's law came from Jerusalem. They gathered around Jesus. \v 2 They saw that some of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were eating food without first washing their hands in the special religious way. \v 3 The Pharisees, like all Jewish people, would not eat unless they had washed their hands in this special way. In this way they kept the rules handed down by their teachers from long ago. \v 4 When they came home from the market, they would not eat until they had washed. They also kept many other rules like these. They washed cups, pitchers, and metal pots in a special way, and even the couches they lay on to eat. \v 5 So the Pharisees and the teachers of God's law asked Jesus, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers not obey the rules our teachers handed down? They eat their food with hands that have not been made clean!"

vi.L: Và những người Pha-ri-si cùng một số thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến tụ họp quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 2 và [họ] đã thấy một số môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn bánh bằng tay ô uế, nghĩa là [tay] chưa rửa \v 3 (vì những người Pha-ri-si và tất cả người Do Thái không ăn nếu không rửa tay bằng nắm tay, giữ theo truyền thống của các trưởng lão, \v 4 và [khi] từ chợ [về], họ không ăn nếu không tẩy rửa mình, và còn nhiều điều khác họ đã nhận để giữ, [như] việc rửa chén, bình, nồi đồng và giường), \v 5 và những người Pha-ri-si cùng các thầy thông giáo hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tại sao các môn đồ của Thầy không bước đi theo truyền thống của các trưởng lão, nhưng ăn bánh bằng tay ô uế?"
vi.B: Những người Pha-ri-si và một số thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến tụ họp quanh Đức Giê-xu. \v 2 Họ đã để ý thấy một số môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn bằng tay ô uế, tức là tay chưa rửa. \v 3 (Những người Pha-ri-si, và cả mọi người Do Thái, không ăn nếu chưa rửa tay theo nghi thức; như thế họ giữ truyền thống của các trưởng lão. \v 4 Khi đi chợ về, họ cũng không ăn nếu chưa tẩy rửa. Họ còn giữ nhiều tập tục khác đã được truyền lại cho họ, như việc rửa chén, bình, nồi đồng và cả ghế dài để nằm ăn.) \v 5 Vì vậy, những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy thông giáo hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Tại sao môn đồ của Thầy không sống theo truyền thống của các trưởng lão, mà lại ăn bằng tay ô uế?"
vi.R: Có mấy người Pha-ri-si và mấy thầy dạy luật từ Giê-ru-sa-lem đến. Họ tụ họp quanh Đức Giê-xu. \v 2 Họ thấy một số môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ăn mà không rửa tay trước theo cách thức tôn giáo đặc biệt. \v 3 Người Pha-ri-si, cũng như mọi người Do Thái, không ăn nếu chưa rửa tay theo cách đặc biệt ấy. Làm như vậy là họ giữ những luật lệ do các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại. \v 4 Khi đi chợ về, họ không ăn cho đến khi đã tẩy rửa. Họ còn giữ nhiều luật lệ khác giống như thế. Họ rửa chén, bình và nồi bằng kim loại theo một cách đặc biệt, và rửa cả những chiếc ghế dài họ nằm khi ăn. \v 5 Vì vậy, những người Pha-ri-si và các thầy dạy luật hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Tại sao môn đồ của Thầy không vâng theo những luật lệ các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại? Họ ăn bằng tay chưa được làm cho tinh sạch!"

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파 사람들과, 예루살렘에서 온 율법학자들 가운데 몇 사람이 그분께로 모여든다. \v 2 그들은 그분의 제자들 가운데 몇 사람이 부정한 손, 곧 씻지 않은 손으로 빵을 먹는 것을 보았다. \v 3 (바리새파 사람들과 모든 유대인은 장로들의 전통을 지켜서, 주먹으로 손을 씻지 않으면 먹지 않는다. \v 4 또 시장에서 [돌아오면] 몸을 씻지 않고는 먹지 않는다. 그 밖에도 그들이 지키도록 전해 받은 것이 많이 있는데, 잔과 단지와 놋그릇과 침상을 씻는 일이다.) \v 5 그래서 바리새파 사람들과 율법학자들이 그분께 묻는다. "왜 당신의 제자들은 장로들의 전통을 따라 행하지 않고, 부정한 손으로 빵을 먹습니까?"
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들과, 예루살렘에서 내려온 율법학자 몇 사람이 예수 주위에 모여들었다. \v 2 그들은 예수의 제자들 가운데 몇 사람이 부정한 손, 곧 씻지 않은 손으로 음식을 먹는 것을 보았다. \v 3 (바리새파 사람들뿐 아니라 모든 유대인은 장로들의 전통을 지켜서, 정해진 방식대로 손을 씻지 않으면 음식을 먹지 않는다. \v 4 시장에서 돌아오면 먼저 몸을 씻지 않고는 먹지 않는다. 그 밖에도 그들이 물려받아 지키는 관습이 많은데, 잔과 단지와 놋그릇과 식사 때 기대는 침상을 씻는 일 같은 것이다.) \v 5 그래서 바리새파 사람들과 율법학자들이 예수께 물었다. "왜 당신의 제자들은 장로들의 전통대로 살지 않습니까? 왜 부정한 손으로 음식을 먹습니까?"
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들과 율법을 가르치는 선생 몇 사람이 예루살렘에서 왔다. 그들이 예수 주위에 모였다. \v 2 그들은 예수의 제자 몇 사람이 손을 씻지 않고 음식을 먹는 것을 보았다. 종교 규칙에 따라 특별한 방식으로 손을 씻어야 하는데, 그렇게 하지 않은 것이다. \v 3 바리새파 사람들은, 다른 모든 유대인처럼, 이 특별한 방식으로 손을 씻지 않으면 음식을 먹지 않았다. 그렇게 해서 오래전 선생들이 물려준 규칙을 지켰다. \v 4 시장에 갔다가 집에 돌아오면, 씻기 전에는 먹지 않았다. 이런 규칙이 그 밖에도 많았다. 그들은 잔과 주전자와 쇠붙이 그릇을 특별한 방식으로 씻었고, 음식을 먹을 때 기대어 눕는 자리까지 씻었다. \v 5 그래서 바리새파 사람들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들이 예수께 물었다. "왜 당신의 제자들은 옛 선생들이 물려준 규칙을 지키지 않습니까? 왜 깨끗하게 씻지 않은 손으로 음식을 먹습니까?"

es.L: Y se reúnen junto a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los fariseos y algunos de los escribas que habían venido de Jerusalén, \v 2 y habían visto que algunos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comen el pan con manos impuras, es decir, sin lavar \v 3 (porque los fariseos y todos los judíos no comen si no se lavan las manos con el puño, aferrándose a la tradición de los ancianos, \v 4 y [al volver] de la plaza no comen si no se lavan, y hay muchas otras cosas que recibieron para guardar: lavamientos de copas, de jarras, de vasijas de bronce y de lechos), \v 5 y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntan los fariseos y los escribas: «¿Por qué no andan {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos conforme a la tradición de los ancianos, sino que comen el pan con manos impuras?».
es.B: Los fariseos se reunieron en torno a Jesús, junto con algunos escribas que habían venido de Jerusalén. \v 2 Habían notado que algunos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comían con manos impuras, es decir, sin lavárselas. \v 3 (Los fariseos, y en realidad todos los judíos, no comen sin antes lavarse las manos con un lavado ritual, y así guardan la tradición de los ancianos. \v 4 Cuando vuelven del mercado, no comen sin lavarse primero. Y guardan muchas otras costumbres que les fueron transmitidas, como lavar copas, jarras, ollas de bronce y los divanes donde se reclinan para comer). \v 5 Así que los fariseos y los escribas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no viven según la tradición de los ancianos? ¿Por qué comen con manos impuras?».
es.R: Algunos fariseos y algunos maestros de la ley vinieron de Jerusalén y se reunieron alrededor de Jesús. \v 2 Vieron que algunos de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos comían sin haberse lavado antes las manos con el lavado religioso especial. \v 3 Los fariseos, como todos los judíos, no comían si no se habían lavado las manos de esa manera especial. Así cumplían las reglas que les habían dejado sus maestros de tiempos antiguos. \v 4 Cuando volvían del mercado, no comían hasta haberse lavado. Además cumplían muchas otras reglas parecidas. Lavaban de una manera especial las copas, las jarras y las ollas de metal, y hasta los divanes en los que se recostaban para comer. \v 5 Entonces los fariseos y los maestros de la ley {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron a Jesús: «¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos no obedecen las reglas que nos dejaron nuestros maestros? ¡Comen con las manos sin purificar!».

fr.L: Et les Pharisiens et quelques-uns des scribes venus de Jérusalem se rassemblent auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \v 2 et ayant vu que quelques-uns de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples mangent les pains avec des mains souillées, c’est-à-dire non lavées \v 3 (car les Pharisiens et tous les Juifs ne mangent pas sans s’être lavé les mains avec le poing, attachés à la tradition des anciens, \v 4 et [au retour] du marché, ils ne mangent pas sans s’être lavés, et il y a beaucoup d’autres choses qu’ils ont reçues pour les observer : lavages de coupes, de cruches, de vases de bronze et de lits), \v 5 et les Pharisiens et les scribes {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogent : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne marchent-ils pas selon la tradition des anciens, mais mangent-ils le pain avec des mains souillées ? »
fr.B: Les Pharisiens se rassemblèrent autour de Jésus, avec quelques scribes venus de Jérusalem. \v 2 Ils avaient remarqué que certains de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples prenaient leur repas avec des mains impures, c’est-à-dire non lavées. \v 3 (Les Pharisiens, comme d’ailleurs tous les Juifs, ne mangent pas sans s’être d’abord lavé les mains selon le rite ; ils restent ainsi fidèles à la tradition des anciens. \v 4 Quand ils rentrent du marché, ils ne mangent pas avant de s’être lavés. Ils observent encore bien d’autres coutumes qui leur ont été transmises, comme le lavage des coupes, des cruches, des pots de bronze et des lits de table.) \v 5 Les Pharisiens et les scribes {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} posèrent donc cette question : « Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples ne vivent-ils pas selon la tradition des anciens ? Pourquoi mangent-ils avec des mains impures ? »
fr.R: Des Pharisiens et des spécialistes de la Loi sont venus de Jérusalem. Ils se sont rassemblés autour de Jésus. \v 2 Ils ont vu que certains de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples mangeaient sans s’être lavé les mains de la façon prévue par la religion. \v 3 Les Pharisiens, comme tous les Juifs, ne mangeaient pas avant de s’être lavé les mains de cette façon spéciale. Ainsi, ils obéissaient aux règles transmises par leurs maîtres d’autrefois. \v 4 Quand ils revenaient du marché, ils ne mangeaient pas avant de s’être lavés. Ils suivaient aussi beaucoup d’autres règles de ce genre. Ils lavaient d’une façon spéciale les coupes, les cruches et les pots en métal, et même les lits sur lesquels ils s’allongeaient pour manger. \v 5 Alors les Pharisiens et les spécialistes de la Loi ont demandé à Jésus : « Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples n’obéissent pas aux règles que nos maîtres d’autrefois nous ont transmises ? Ils mangent avec des mains qui n’ont pas été purifiées ! »

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo na baadhi ya waandishi waliokuja kutoka Yerusalemu wanakusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, \v 2 nao walikuwa wameona kwamba baadhi ya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wanakula mikate [yao] kwa mikono najisi, yaani, isiyooshwa \v 3 (kwa maana Mafarisayo na Wayahudi wote hawali wasiponawa mikono kwa ngumi, wakishika mapokeo ya wazee, \v 4 na [wakitoka] sokoni hawali wasipojiosha, na kuna mambo mengine mengi waliyopokea ili wayashike: kuosha vikombe na mitungi na vyombo vya shaba na vitanda), \v 5 na Mafarisayo na waandishi wanamwuliza, "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawaenendi kufuatana na mapokeo ya wazee, bali wanakula mikate [yao] kwa mikono najisi?"
sw.B: Mafarisayo walikusanyika kumzunguka Yesu, pamoja na baadhi ya waandishi waliokuwa wamekuja kutoka Yerusalemu. \v 2 Walikuwa wameona kwamba baadhi ya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakila chakula kwa mikono najisi, yaani, mikono isiyooshwa. \v 3 (Mafarisayo, na kwa kweli Wayahudi wote, hawali chakula bila kunawa mikono kwa taratibu za kidini; kwa njia hiyo wanashika mapokeo ya wazee. \v 4 Wanapotoka sokoni hawali kabla ya kujiosha. Pia wanashikilia desturi nyingine nyingi walizopokezwa, kama vile kuosha vikombe, mitungi, vyungu vya shaba na vitanda vya kuegemea wakati wa kula.) \v 5 Basi Mafarisayo na waandishi wakamwuliza Yesu, "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawaishi kufuatana na mapokeo ya wazee? Kwa nini wanakula kwa mikono najisi?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo na baadhi ya walimu wa sheria walikuja kutoka Yerusalemu. Wakakusanyika kumzunguka Yesu. \v 2 Waliona kwamba baadhi ya wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakila chakula bila kwanza kunawa mikono kwa namna maalumu ya kidini. \v 3 Mafarisayo, kama Wayahudi wote, hawakula chakula kabla ya kunawa mikono kwa namna hiyo maalumu. Kwa njia hiyo walishika kanuni walizorithi kutoka kwa walimu wao wa zamani. \v 4 Waliporudi kutoka sokoni, hawakula mpaka wamejiosha kwanza. Walishika pia kanuni nyingine nyingi kama hizo. Waliosha vikombe, mitungi na vyungu vya shaba kwa namna maalumu, na hata vitanda walivyoegemea wakati wa kula. \v 5 Basi Mafarisayo na walimu wa sheria wakamwuliza Yesu, "Kwa nini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} hawashiki kanuni ambazo walimu wetu wa zamani walitupa? Wanakula chakula kwa mikono ambayo haijatakaswa!"

pt.L: E os fariseus e alguns dos escribas que tinham vindo de Jerusalém se reúnem junto {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, \v 2 e [eles] tinham visto que alguns dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos comem [o] pão com mãos contaminadas, isto é, não lavadas \v 3 (pois os fariseus e todos os judeus não comem se não lavarem as mãos com o punho, apegando-se à tradição dos anciãos, \v 4 e, [voltando] da praça do mercado, não comem se não se lavarem; e há muitas outras coisas que receberam para guardar: lavagens de copos, de jarros, de vasilhas de bronze e de leitos), \v 5 e os fariseus e os escribas {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} perguntam: "Por que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos não andam segundo a tradição dos anciãos, mas comem [o] pão com mãos contaminadas?"
pt.B: Os fariseus se reuniram em volta de Jesus, junto com alguns escribas que tinham vindo de Jerusalém. \v 2 Eles tinham notado que alguns dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos comiam com mãos impuras, isto é, sem lavá-las. \v 3 (Os fariseus, e na verdade todos os judeus, não comem sem antes fazer uma lavagem ritual das mãos, e assim guardam a tradição dos anciãos. \v 4 Quando voltam do mercado, não comem sem antes se lavar. E guardam muitos outros costumes que lhes foram transmitidos, como a lavagem de copos, jarros, vasilhas de bronze e leitos de refeição.) \v 5 Então os fariseus e os escribas {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} fizeram uma pergunta: "Por que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} discípulos não vivem segundo a tradição dos anciãos? Por que comem com mãos impuras?"
pt.R: Alguns fariseus e alguns mestres da Lei vieram de Jerusalém. Eles se reuniram em volta de Jesus. \v 2 Eles viram que alguns dos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores estavam comendo sem antes lavar as mãos do jeito especial que a religião deles mandava. \v 3 Os fariseus, como todos os judeus, só comiam depois de lavar as mãos desse jeito especial. Assim eles obedeciam às regras que os mestres deles, de muito tempo atrás, tinham deixado. \v 4 Quando voltavam do mercado, eles só comiam depois de se lavar. Eles também obedeciam a muitas outras regras parecidas. Lavavam de um jeito especial os copos, os jarros e as panelas de metal, e até os leitos em que se deitavam para comer. \v 5 Então os fariseus e os mestres da Lei perguntaram a Jesus: "Por que os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} seguidores não obedecem às regras que os nossos mestres nos deixaram? Eles comem com mãos que não foram purificadas!"

am.L: ፈሪሳውያንና ከኢየሩሳሌም የመጡ አንዳንድ ጸሐፍትም ወደ እርሱ ይሰበሰባሉ፤ \v 2 ከደቀ መዛሙርቱም አንዳንዶቹ በረከሱ እጆች፣ ማለትም ባልታጠቡ [እጆች]፣ እንጀራ ሲበሉ አይተው ነበር \v 3 (ፈሪሳውያንና አይሁድ ሁሉ የሽማግሌዎችን ወግ ይዘው እጃቸውን በጡጫ ካልታጠቡ አይበሉምና፤ \v 4 ከገበያም [ሲመለሱ] ካልታጠቡ አይበሉም፤ ሊይዟቸው የተቀበሏቸው ሌሎች ብዙ ነገሮችም አሉ፤ የጽዋዎችና የማሰሮዎች የነሐስ ዕቃዎችና የአልጋዎችም መታጠብ)፤ \v 5 ፈሪሳውያንና ጸሐፍትም እንዲህ ብለው ይጠይቁታል፦ «ደቀ መዛሙርትህ ለምን እንደ ሽማግሌዎች ወግ አይመላለሱም፤ ነገር ግን በረከሱ እጆች እንጀራ ይበላሉ?»
am.B: ፈሪሳውያንና ከኢየሩሳሌም የመጡ አንዳንድ የሕግ መምህራን በኢየሱስ ዙሪያ ተሰበሰቡ። \v 2 ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ አንዳንዶቹ በረከሱ እጆች፣ ማለትም ባልታጠቡ እጆች፣ ምግብ ሲበሉ አይተው ነበር። \v 3 (ፈሪሳውያንና አይሁድ ሁሉ እጃቸውን በሥርዓቱ መሠረት ካልታጠቡ አይበሉም፤ በዚህም የሽማግሌዎችን ወግ ይጠብቃሉ። \v 4 ከገበያ ሲመለሱም ሳይታጠቡ አይበሉም። እንዲሁም ጽዋዎችን፣ ማሰሮዎችን፣ የነሐስ ዕቃዎችንና የመመገቢያ መደቦችን ማጠብን የመሳሰሉ፣ የተቀበሏቸውና የሚጠብቋቸው ሌሎች ብዙ ልማዶች አሏቸው።) \v 5 ስለዚህ ፈሪሳውያንና የሕግ መምህራን እንዲህ ብለው ጠየቁት፦ «ደቀ መዛሙርትህ ለምን በሽማግሌዎች ወግ አይኖሩም? ለምንስ በረከሱ እጆች ይበላሉ?»
am.R: አንዳንድ ፈሪሳውያንና የሕግ መምህራን ከኢየሩሳሌም መጡ። በኢየሱስም ዙሪያ ተሰበሰቡ። \v 2 ከደቀ መዛሙርቱ አንዳንዶቹ እጃቸውን በታዘዘው ሃይማኖታዊ ሥርዓት ሳይታጠቡ ምግብ ሲበሉ አዩ። \v 3 ፈሪሳውያን፣ እንደ ሌሎቹ አይሁድ ሁሉ፣ እጃቸውን በዚህ ልዩ ሥርዓት ካልታጠቡ አይበሉም ነበር። በዚህም የጥንት መሪዎቻቸው ያስተላለፉላቸውን ሥርዓት ይጠብቁ ነበር። \v 4 ከገበያ ወደ ቤት ሲመለሱም ካልታጠቡ አይበሉም ነበር። እንደዚህ ያሉ ሌሎች ብዙ ሥርዓቶችንም ይጠብቁ ነበር። ጽዋዎችን፣ ማሰሮዎችንና የብረት ድስቶችን በልዩ ሥርዓት ያጥቡ ነበር፤ ለመመገብ የሚደገፉባቸውን መደቦች እንኳ ያጥቡ ነበር። \v 5 ስለዚህ ፈሪሳውያንና የሕግ መምህራን ኢየሱስን እንዲህ ብለው ጠየቁት፦ «ደቀ መዛሙርትህ የጥንት መሪዎቻችን ያስተላለፉልንን ሥርዓት ለምን አይጠብቁም? እጃቸውን ሳያነጹ ምግብ ይበላሉ!»

ru.L: И собираются к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} фарисеи и некоторые из книжников, пришедшие из Иерусалима, \v 2 и увидели, что некоторые из {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} учеников едят хлеб нечистыми, то есть немытыми, руками \v 3 (ведь фарисеи и все иудеи, если не вымоют рук горстью, не едят, держась предания старейшин, \v 4 и, [придя] с рынка, если не омоются, не едят; и много другого есть, что они приняли соблюдать: омовения чаш, и кувшинов, и медной посуды, и лож), \v 5 и спрашивают {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} фарисеи и книжники: «Почему {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} ученики не ходят по преданию старейшин, но едят хлеб нечистыми руками?»
ru.B: Вокруг Иисуса собрались фарисеи и несколько учителей Закона, пришедших из Иерусалима. \v 2 Они заметили, что некоторые из {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} учеников едят нечистыми, то есть немытыми, руками. \v 3 (Фарисеи, да и все иудеи, не садятся есть, пока не совершат над руками обрядового омовения: так они соблюдают предание старейшин. \v 4 Придя с рынка, они не едят, не омывшись. Они держатся и многих других обычаев, которые им передали, например омовения чаш, кувшинов, медной посуды и лож для трапезы.) \v 5 Поэтому фарисеи и учители Закона спросили {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}: «Почему {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} ученики не живут по преданию старейшин? Почему они едят нечистыми руками?»
ru.R: Несколько фарисеев и учителей Закона пришли из Иерусалима. Они собрались вокруг Иисуса. \v 2 Они увидели, что некоторые из {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} учеников едят, не помыв сначала руки особым религиозным образом. \v 3 Фарисеи, как и все иудеи, не ели, пока не помоют руки таким особым образом. Так они соблюдали правила, которые передали им учителя давних времён. \v 4 Когда они приходили домой с рынка, они не ели, пока не совершат омовение. Они соблюдали и много других подобных правил. Они особым образом мыли чашки, кувшины и медные котлы, и даже ложа, на которых возлежали за едой. \v 5 Поэтому фарисеи и учители Закона спросили Иисуса: «Почему {{deity_pronoun:твои|Твои}} ученики не соблюдают правила, которые передали нам наши учителя? Они едят руками, которые не стали чистыми!»

hi.L: और फ़रीसी और कुछ शास्त्री, जो यरूशलेम से आए थे, उनके पास इकट्ठे होते हैं, \v 2 और [उन्होंने] देखा था कि उनके कुछ चेले अशुद्ध, अर्थात् बिना धोए, हाथों से रोटी खाते हैं \v 3 (क्योंकि फ़रीसी और सब यहूदी पुरनियों की परंपरा को मानते हुए, जब तक मुट्ठी से हाथ न धो लें, नहीं खाते, \v 4 और बाज़ार से [आकर], जब तक अपने आप को न धो लें, नहीं खाते; और बहुत-सी और बातें हैं जिन्हें मानने के लिए उन्होंने ग्रहण किया है, जैसे कटोरों और घड़ों और ताँबे के बरतनों और पलंगों को धोना), \v 5 और फ़रीसी और शास्त्री उनसे पूछते हैं, "आपके चेले पुरनियों की परंपरा के अनुसार क्यों नहीं चलते, बल्कि अशुद्ध हाथों से रोटी खाते हैं?"
hi.B: फ़रीसी, और व्यवस्था के कुछ शिक्षक जो यरूशलेम से आए थे, यीशु के पास इकट्ठे हुए। \v 2 उन्होंने देखा था कि उनके कुछ चेले अशुद्ध हाथों से, यानी बिना धोए हाथों से, भोजन कर रहे थे। \v 3 (फ़रीसी, और वास्तव में सब यहूदी, जब तक रीति के अनुसार हाथ न धो लें, भोजन नहीं करते। इस तरह वे बुज़ुर्ग अगुवों से चली आ रही परंपरा को मानते हैं। \v 4 बाज़ार से लौटकर वे पहले नहाए-धोए बिना नहीं खाते। और भी बहुत-सी रीतियाँ हैं जो उन्हें सौंपी गई हैं और जिन्हें वे मानते हैं, जैसे कटोरों, घड़ों, ताँबे के बरतनों और भोजन के आसनों को धोना।) \v 5 इसलिए फ़रीसियों और व्यवस्था के शिक्षकों ने उनसे पूछा, "आपके चेले बुज़ुर्ग अगुवों की परंपरा के अनुसार क्यों नहीं चलते? वे अशुद्ध हाथों से भोजन क्यों करते हैं?"
hi.R: कुछ फ़रीसी और व्यवस्था के कुछ शिक्षक यरूशलेम से आए। वे यीशु के चारों ओर इकट्ठे हो गए। \v 2 उन्होंने देखा कि यीशु के कुछ चेले ख़ास धार्मिक रीति से हाथ धोए बिना खाना खा रहे थे। \v 3 फ़रीसी, और सब यहूदी लोग भी, जब तक इस ख़ास रीति से हाथ न धो लें, खाना नहीं खाते थे। इस तरह वे उन नियमों को मानते थे जो उनके पुराने अगुवे उन्हें सौंप गए थे। \v 4 जब वे बाज़ार से घर आते, तो जब तक नहा-धो न लें, खाना नहीं खाते थे। वे ऐसे और भी बहुत-से नियम मानते थे। वे कटोरों, घड़ों और धातु के बरतनों को ख़ास रीति से धोते थे, यहाँ तक कि उन आसनों को भी जिन पर वे टेक लगाकर खाना खाते थे। \v 5 इसलिए फ़रीसियों और व्यवस्था के शिक्षकों ने यीशु से पूछा, "आपके चेले उन नियमों को क्यों नहीं मानते जो हमारे पुराने अगुवे हमें सौंप गए हैं? वे बिना शुद्ध किए हाथों से खाना खाते हैं!"

uk.L: І збираються до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} фарисеї та деякі з книжників, що прийшли з Єрусалима, \v 2 і побачили, що деякі з {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учнів їдять хліб нечистими руками, тобто немитими \v 3 (бо фарисеї і всі юдеї не їдять, якщо не помиють рук кулаком, тримаючись передання старших, \v 4 і [прийшовши] з ринку, не їдять, якщо не обмиються, і є багато іншого, що вони прийняли, щоб того триматися: обмивання чаш, і глеків, і мідного посуду, і лож), \v 5 і питають {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} фарисеї та книжники: «Чому {{deity_pronoun:твої|Твої}} учні не поводяться за переданням старших, а їдять хліб нечистими руками?»
uk.B: Біля Ісуса зібралися фарисеї разом із деякими учителями Закону, що прийшли з Єрусалима. \v 2 Вони помітили, що деякі з {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учнів їдять нечистими, тобто необмитими, руками. \v 3 (Фарисеї, та й усі юдеї, не сідають їсти, доки обрядово не обмиють рук, і так дотримуються передання старших. \v 4 Повернувшись із ринку, вони не їдять, не обмившись. Є й багато інших звичаїв, які їм передано і яких вони тримаються: обмивання чаш, глеків, мідних горщиків і лож, на яких сидять при трапезі.) \v 5 Тож фарисеї та учителі Закону запитали {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}: «Чому {{deity_pronoun:твої|Твої}} учні не живуть за переданням старших? Чому вони їдять нечистими руками?»
uk.R: З Єрусалима прийшли деякі фарисеї та учителі Божого Закону. Вони зібралися навколо Ісуса. \v 2 Вони побачили, що деякі з {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учнів їдять, не обмивши перед тим рук особливим релігійним способом. \v 3 Фарисеї, як і всі юдеї, не їли, доки не обмиють рук у такий особливий спосіб. Так вони дотримувалися правил, які передали їм давні вчителі. \v 4 Коли вони приходили з ринку, то не їли, доки не обмиються. Вони дотримувалися ще багатьох таких правил. Вони по-особливому мили чаші, глеки й металеві горщики, і навіть ложа, на яких лежали під час їжі. \v 5 Тож фарисеї та учителі Закону запитали Ісуса: «Чому {{deity_pronoun:твої|Твої}} учні не дотримуються правил, які передали нам наші вчителі? Вони їдять руками, які не очищені!»

ja.L: そして、ファリサイ派の人々と、エルサレムから来た律法学者たちの何人かが、イエスのもとに集まる。\v 2 そして、彼らは、イエスの弟子たちの何人かが汚れた手、すなわち洗っていない手で[自分たちの]パンを食べているのを見た。\v 3 （ファリサイ派の人々も、すべてのユダヤ人も、長老たちの言い伝えを固く守っていて、拳で手を洗わなければ食事をしない。\v 4 また、市場から[帰ったときには]、身を洗わなければ食事をしない。そのほかにも、杯や水差しや銅の器や寝椅子を洗うことなど、守るように受け継いだことが数多くある。）\v 5 そして、ファリサイ派の人々と律法学者たちはイエスに尋ねる。「なぜ、あなたの弟子たちは長老たちの言い伝えに従って歩まず、汚れた手でパンを食べるのか？」
ja.B: ファリサイ派の人々が、エルサレムから来た何人かの律法学者たちと一緒に、イエスのもとに集まって来た。\v 2 彼らは、イエスの弟子たちの何人かが汚れた手、つまり洗っていない手で食事をしているのに気づいていた。\v 3 （ファリサイ派の人々をはじめ、ユダヤ人は皆、定められた仕方で手を洗ってからでなければ食事をしない。こうして長老たちの言い伝えを守っているのである。\v 4 市場から戻ったときも、身を清めてからでなければ食事をしない。このほかにも、杯や水差しや銅の鍋や食事用の寝椅子を洗うことなど、受け継いで守っている習わしがたくさんある。）\v 5 そこで、ファリサイ派の人々と律法学者たちはイエスに問いただした。「なぜ、あなたの弟子たちは長老たちの言い伝えに従って生活しないのか？なぜ汚れた手で食事をするのか？」
ja.R: エルサレムから、何人かのファリサイ派の人々と律法の先生たちがやって来ました。彼らはイエスの周りに集まりました。\v 2 彼らは、イエスの弟子たちの何人かが、決められた特別な仕方で手を洗わずに食事をしているのを見ました。\v 3 ファリサイ派の人々は、ほかのユダヤ人たちと同じように、この特別な仕方で手を洗ってからでなければ食事をしませんでした。こうして、昔の先生たちから伝えられた決まりを守っていたのです。\v 4 市場から帰ったときも、体を洗ってからでなければ食事をしませんでした。ほかにも、これと同じような決まりをたくさん守っていました。杯や水差しや金属の鍋を特別な仕方で洗い、食事のときに横になる寝椅子まで洗いました。\v 5 そこで、ファリサイ派の人々と律法の先生たちはイエスに尋ねました。「なぜ、あなたの弟子たちは、昔の先生たちから伝えられた決まりを守らないのか？清めていない手で食事をしているではないか！」

decisions.choice: are gathered, question: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they gathered, and they asked.

decisions.choice: defiled hands: hands that had not been washed by the ritual, so counted unclean, not dirty
decisions.reason: The word means common, ordinary, and so not set apart as clean. The washing was a religious rite, not a matter of hygiene. Mark explains this to readers who did not know Jewish custom.

decisions.choice: Mark stops the story to explain Jewish washing customs
decisions.reason: Verses 3-4 are Mark's note to his readers, many of whom were not Jews. The sentence that began in verse 1 is broken off and picked up again in verse 5.

decisions.choice: with the fist: a particular ritual way of washing, whose exact form is uncertain
alternatives: with a cupped handful of water
decisions.reason: The word means a fist. It may describe pouring water over the hands held in a fist, rubbing one fist in the other palm, or washing up to the wrist. All agree it names a set way of washing.

decisions.choice: with the fist, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "often" and a few leave the word out, perhaps because scribes found "with the fist" hard to understand. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the tradition of the elders: rules taught by earlier teachers and passed on by word of mouth
decisions.reason: The elders here are teachers of past generations. Their rulings, added to the law of Moses, were held by the Pharisees to be binding. The washing of hands before ordinary meals is not commanded in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: from the marketplace: when they come back from the market, they wash before eating
alternatives: they do not eat food from the market unless they wash it
decisions.reason: The words can be read either way. Most likely contact with many people at the market was thought to make a person unclean.

decisions.choice: wash themselves, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read "sprinkle themselves". The SBLGNT reads the verb that means to wash or dip, the word from which baptize comes. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and couches: in the SBLGNT text
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts do not have "and couches", perhaps because scribes thought it strange to wash couches. The couches were those people reclined on to eat. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: give their hands a ritual washing
alternatives: wash their hands with the fist
decisions.reason: The exact sense of "with the fist" is unknown. Balanced gives what is certain: a set religious washing.

decisions.choice: the rules handed down by their teachers from long ago; the couches they lay on to eat
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the elders were and what couches were washed.

decisions.choice: "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "các thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes
alternatives: "các thầy dạy luật" at every level
decisions.reason: The forms the Vietnamese John already uses (8:3): the traditional title at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable a plain description of what these men did, teaching the law of Moses. "Kinh sư" is the Catholic word.

decisions.choice: "truyền thống của các trưởng lão" (L, B); "những luật lệ do các bậc thầy đời xưa truyền lại" (R)
alternatives: "lời truyền khẩu của các bậc trưởng thượng"
decisions.reason: "Truyền thống" is the ordinary word for teaching handed down; "trưởng lão" keeps the Greek "elders". Readable says who the elders were, teachers of earlier times, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "tụ họp", "hỏi" with no "đã" (L)
decisions.reason: Mark tells these events in the present tense. Vietnamese verbs have no tense, so Literal keeps the vivid present by leaving out "đã", as the Vietnamese John does; the same holds for the other present-tense verbs of this chapter (7:18, 7:28, 7:32, 7:34).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("모여든다", "묻는다", "말씀하신다"), through chapter 7
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (7:1, 7:5, 7:18, 7:28, 7:32, 7:34); Balanced and Readable use the past, as in the Korean of chapter 3. Recorded once for the chapter.

decisions.choice: "부정한 손" for the defiled (common) hands (L, B), explained in Readable; "장로들의 전통" (L, B), "오래전 선생들이 물려준 규칙" (R)
decisions.reason: The hands are ritually unclean, not dirty, so "부정한" (unclean in the religious sense) is used rather than "더러운"; the same root carries through "부정하게 하다" in 7:15-23. "장로들" keeps the word used for the elders of 8:31; Readable says who they were.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees and scribes question Jesus in 합쇼체 but call him "당신", not "선생님"
alternatives: "선생님" as in the crowd's speech in 3:32
decisions.reason: The scene is hostile: they speak formally (합쇼체), as officials would, but keep their distance with "당신", as the unclean spirits do in 3:11. The style guide (section 4) allows this with a decision.

decisions.choice: present tense (L); past tense (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1 and John: Mark often tells his story in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it ("se reúnen", "preguntan"); Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories do. This applies throughout the chapter. Plural "you" is the ustedes / vosotros setting, and every pronoun for Jesus that Spanish writes as a separate word takes the deity_pronoun setting, by the rule set for Mark at 1:2.

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22: "escribas" is the word Spanish Bibles use; Readable says what these men were.

decisions.choice: manos impuras (L, B); sin purificar (R)
decisions.reason: The hands were not dirty but ritually unclean (meaning decision m2); Spanish "impuras" says that, where "sucias" would not.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (B), with Literal keeping Mark’s present tense ("se rassemblent", "interrogent") and using the passé simple elsewhere; passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole of Mark 7. The passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken and school French. Literal keeps the present wherever Mark tells a past event in the present (7:1, 5, 18, 28, 32, 34), as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "des mains souillées" (L); "des mains impures" (B); "des mains qui n’ont pas été purifiées" (R)
decisions.reason: The hands were ritually unclean, not dirty (meaning decision on "defiled hands"). "Sales" would say dirt; Literal says "souillées", the word it keeps for the verb "defile" in 7:15-23, and Balanced "impures", the word it uses there for "make unclean".

decisions.choice: "les scribes" (L, B); "les spécialistes de la Loi" (R)
decisions.reason: As in French John (8:3): "scribe" today suggests a copyist, so Readable says what they were; "maîtres de la Loi" would clash with "Maître" as an address to Jesus, and "docteurs" now means physicians. Used for Mark as a whole.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanakusanyika, wanamwuliza); past at Balanced and Readable (walikusanyika, wakamwuliza)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present (meaning decision). Literal keeps it, as in the earlier chapters; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past with -li- and -ka-, as written Swahili narrative does. This holds for the whole of chapter 7.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (kwake, wake, wako)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in John and the earlier chapters of Mark: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb ("wanamwuliza", "walikusanyika kumzunguka"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer setting spans than English in this chapter.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
alternatives: walimu wa sheria at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark 1:22 and John 8:3: "waandishi" is the established Swahili name for the scribes; Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of God's law".

decisions.choice: mikono najisi (unclean hands)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says the hands were ritually unclean, not dirty. "Najisi" is the Swahili word for what is ritually unclean, while "michafu" would mean only that they needed soap. The same word, and the verb "kutia unajisi" / "kufanya najisi", carries 7:15-23.

decisions.choice: wanafunzi (disciples) at every level
decisions.reason: As in John and the earlier chapters of Mark, "wanafunzi" is plain enough for Readable, where the English Readable says "followers".

decisions.choice: mãos contaminadas (L); mãos impuras (B)
decisions.reason: The hands are not dirty but ritually unclean (m2). "Sujas" would suggest hygiene. Literal says "contaminadas", which matches "contaminar" for the related verb in 7:15-23 (as in Matthew 15:11-20); Balanced says "impuras", the word Balanced uses for "unclean" in the same passage.

decisions.choice: leitos (L); leitos de refeição (B); os leitos em que se deitavam para comer (R)
decisions.reason: "Sofá" is a modern living-room word, and "cama" would suggest a bed for sleeping. "Leito" is the older word for a couch to lie on, and Balanced and Readable say what it was used for, since people reclined to eat (m9).

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span in Amharic
alternatives: A deity_pronoun span, as in the English
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic; pronouns and verb endings for Jesus are written plainly in every level of this passage.

decisions.choice: "ጸሐፍት" (L); "የሕግ መምህራን" (teachers of the Law, B, R)
decisions.reason: The scribes were teachers of the Law, not copyists. Literal keeps the traditional "ጸሐፍት"; Balanced and Readable say what they were, as in Matthew.

decisions.choice: "книжники" (L); "учители Закона" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled term: scribes were teachers of the Law, not copyists.

decisions.choice: "ученики"
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "ученики" at every level, Readable included.

decisions.choice: "горстью"
decisions.reason: The exact sense of "with the fist" is unknown. Literal keeps a picture of the hand, "горстью" (with a cupped hand), which reads naturally in Russian; Balanced and Readable say only what is certain, a set religious washing.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change and the Hindi has no deity_pronoun spans, for Jesus here or for God speaking in Isaiah (7:6-7). Respect for Jesus is shown at every level by the honorific third person (वे, उन्होंने, उनके) and by आप when people speak to him.

decisions.choice: "शास्त्री" (L); "व्यवस्था के शिक्षक" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term settled for the book: scribes were teachers of the Law.

decisions.choice: "पुरनिए" (L); "बुज़ुर्ग अगुवे" (B); "पुराने अगुवे" (R)
decisions.reason: The book's term for elders, with Readable making plain that teachers of earlier generations are meant, as in Matthew 15:2.

decisions.choice: "मुट्ठी से"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word, whose exact sense is unknown; Balanced and Readable say what is certain, a set religious washing ("रीति के अनुसार").

decisions.choice: "पलंग" (L); "भोजन के आसन" (B, R)
decisions.reason: These are the couches on which people reclined at meals; "खाट" is kept for the mats the sick are carried on (6:55).

decisions.choice: "книжники" (L); "учителі Закону" (B, R)
decisions.reason: They were teachers of the Law, not copyists, as the style guide sets for the whole New Testament; Literal keeps the traditional name.

decisions.choice: "передання старших" (L, B); "правила, які передали давні вчителі" (R)
decisions.reason: The elders here are the teachers of earlier generations, not the town elders ("старійшини"); "передання старших" names rules handed down by word of mouth. Readable says so plainly.

decisions.choice: "集まる", "尋ねる" (L); "集まって来た", "問いただした" (B); "集まりました", "尋ねました" (R)
decisions.reason: Mark tells the past in the present tense for vividness (m1). Literal keeps the present, as it does for Mark's historic presents through 7:1-13; Balanced and Readable narrate in the past, which is how Japanese tells a story.

decisions.choice: "拳で" (L); "定められた仕方で" (B); "特別な仕方で" (R); "長老たちの言い伝え" (L, B), "昔の先生たちから伝えられた決まり" (R)
alternatives: "念入りに" (B), which guesses at one explanation of the word
decisions.reason: The exact form of washing "with the fist" is unknown (m4); Literal keeps the word, Balanced and Readable say only what is certain, a set religious washing. The elders are teachers of earlier generations (m6), which Readable spells out; the same wording returns in 7:5, 7:8-9 and 7:13.

decisions.choice: the Pharisees ask in the plain style ("食べるのか？")
decisions.reason: These men come to challenge Jesus, not to ask a favour; as with Jesus' opponents in John, their speech is plain.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἠσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν, ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Well prophesied Isaiah about you the hypocrites, as it has been written, This people with the lips me honors, but the heart of them far is away from me;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Well did Isaiah prophesy about you hypocrites, as it is written, 'This people honors {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with [their] lips, but their heart is far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}};
en.B: He answered them, "How well Isaiah prophesied about you hypocrites! As it stands written: 'This people gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honor with their lips, while their heart stays far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Jesus answered them, "You are hypocrites. You pretend to be good, but you are not. Isaiah was right about you when he spoke God's message long ago. He wrote down what God said: 'These people say that they honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but it is only words from their lips. Their hearts are far away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Ê-sai đã nói tiên tri đúng về các người, những kẻ giả hình, như có chép rằng: 'Dân này lấy môi tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng lòng họ thì xa cách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}};
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Ê-sai đã nói tiên tri thật đúng về các người, những kẻ đạo đức giả! Như lời đã chép: 'Dân này tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng môi miệng, còn lòng họ thì xa cách {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Các người là những kẻ đạo đức giả. Các người làm ra vẻ tốt lành, nhưng thật ra không phải vậy. Từ xưa, Ê-sai đã nói đúng về các người khi ông truyền lại sứ điệp của Đức Chúa Trời. Ông đã chép lại lời Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Dân này nói rằng họ tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng đó chỉ là lời nói ngoài môi miệng. Lòng họ thì ở xa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "이사야가 너희 위선자들에 대하여 잘 예언하였다. 이렇게 기록되어 있다. '이 백성은 입술로 나를 공경하지만, 그들의 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "이사야가 너희 위선자들을 두고 참 잘 예언했다! 기록된 대로이다. '이 백성은 입술로는 나를 높이지만, 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떠나 있다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "너희는 위선자들이다. 착한 척하지만 실제로는 그렇지 않다. 오래전에 이사야가 하나님의 말씀을 전했는데, 그 말이 너희에게 꼭 들어맞았다. 이사야는 하나님께서 하신 말씀을 이렇게 기록했다. '이 사람들은 나를 공경한다고 말하지만, 그것은 입술에서 나오는 말뿐이다. 그들의 마음은 나에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «Bien profetizó Isaías acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hipócritas, como está escrito: “Este pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra con los labios, pero su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}};
es.B: Él les respondió: «¡Qué bien profetizó Isaías acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hipócritas! Así está escrito: “Este pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra con los labios, pero su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} unos hipócritas. {{plural_you:Aparentan|Aparentáis}} ser buenos, pero no lo {{plural_you:son|sois}}. Isaías tenía razón cuando, hace mucho tiempo, habló de parte de Dios acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Él escribió lo que Dios dijo: “Esta gente dice que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra, pero son solo palabras de sus labios. Su corazón está lejos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Isaïe a bien prophétisé à votre sujet, hypocrites, comme il est écrit : “Ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore avec les lèvres, mais leur cœur se tient loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ;
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Comme Isaïe a bien prophétisé à votre sujet, hypocrites ! Il est écrit en effet : “Ce peuple {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honore de ses lèvres, mais son cœur se tient loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Vous êtes des hypocrites. Vous faites semblant d’être bons, mais vous ne l’êtes pas. Le prophète Isaïe avait raison à votre sujet quand il a transmis le message de Dieu, il y a longtemps. Il a écrit ce que Dieu disait : “Ces gens disent qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}honorent, mais ce ne sont que des mots sur leurs lèvres. Leur cœur est loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Isaya alitabiri vema kuhusu ninyi wanafiki, kama ilivyoandikwa, 'Watu hawa wananipa heshima kwa midomo, lakini moyo wao umekaa mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}};
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Isaya alitabiri sawasawa kabisa kuhusu ninyi wanafiki! Kama ilivyoandikwa: 'Watu hawa hunipa heshima kwa midomo yao, ilhali mioyo yao imekaa mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.
sw.R: Yesu akawajibu, "Ninyi ni wanafiki. Mnajifanya kuwa watu wema, lakini sivyo mlivyo. Zamani nabii Isaya alipotoa ujumbe wa Mungu, alisema kweli kuhusu ninyi. Aliandika maneno haya ya Mungu: 'Watu hawa wanasema kwamba wananiheshimu, lakini ni maneno ya midomo yao tu. Mioyo yao iko mbali {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes disse: "Bem profetizou Isaías a respeito de vocês, hipócritas, como está escrito: 'Este povo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra com os lábios, mas o coração deles está longe de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}};
pt.B: Ele lhes respondeu: "Como Isaías profetizou bem a respeito de vocês, hipócritas! Assim está escrito: 'Com os lábios este povo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honra, mas o coração dele se mantém longe de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "Vocês são hipócritas. Fingem ser bons, mas não são. Isaías estava certo a respeito de vocês quando anunciou a mensagem de Deus muito tempo atrás. Ele escreveu o que Deus disse: 'Essas pessoas dizem que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} honram, mas são só palavras que saem dos lábios delas. O coração delas está longe de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.

am.L: እርሱም አላቸው፦ «ኢሳይያስ ስለ እናንተ ስለ ግብዞች መልካም አድርጎ ትንቢት ተናገረ፤ እንዲህ ተብሎ እንደ ተጻፈ፦ “ይህ ሕዝብ በከንፈሮች ያከብረኛል፤ ልባቸው ግን ከእኔ ርቆ ይገኛል፤
am.B: እርሱም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰላቸው፦ «እናንተ ግብዞች፣ ኢሳይያስ ስለ እናንተ እንዴት በትክክል ትንቢት ተናገረ! እንዲህ ተብሎ ተጽፏልና፦ “እነዚህ ሰዎች በከንፈራቸው ያከብሩኛል፤ ልባቸው ግን ከእኔ ርቆ ይኖራል።
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰላቸው፦ «እናንተ ግብዞች ናችሁ። ጥሩ መስላችሁ ትታያላችሁ፤ ነገር ግን ጥሩዎች አይደላችሁም። ኢሳይያስ ከብዙ ዘመን በፊት የእግዚአብሔርን መልእክት በተናገረ ጊዜ ስለ እናንተ በትክክል ተናገረ። እግዚአብሔር ያለውንም እንዲህ ብሎ ጻፈ፦ “እነዚህ ሰዎች እንደሚያከብሩኝ ይናገራሉ፤ ነገር ግን ይህ የከንፈር ቃል ብቻ ነው። ልባቸው ከእኔ በጣም ሩቅ ነው።

ru.L: Он же сказал им: «Хорошо пророчествовал Исаия о вас, лицемерах, как написано: “Этот народ чтит {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} губами, сердце же их далеко отстоит от {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}};
ru.B: Он ответил им: «Как хорошо пророчествовал о вас, лицемерах, Исаия! Как написано: “Этот народ чтит {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} устами, но сердце его держится далеко от {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}.
ru.R: Иисус ответил им: «Вы лицемеры. Вы притворяетесь хорошими, но вы не такие. Исаия был прав, когда давным-давно передал о вас весть от Бога. Он записал то, что сказал Бог: “Эти люди говорят, что чтут {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, но это лишь слова на их губах. Их сердца далеко от {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}.

hi.L: और उन्होंने उनसे कहा, "यशायाह ने तुम पाखंडियों के विषय में ठीक ही भविष्यद्वाणी की, जैसा लिखा है, 'ये लोग होंठों से मेरा सम्मान करते हैं, परंतु उनका हृदय मुझसे बहुत दूर है;
hi.B: उन्होंने उन्हें उत्तर दिया, "यशायाह ने तुम पाखंडियों के विषय में कितनी ठीक भविष्यद्वाणी की! जैसा लिखा है: 'ये लोग अपने होंठों से मेरा सम्मान करते हैं, पर उनका हृदय मुझसे दूर ही रहता है।
hi.R: यीशु ने उन्हें जवाब दिया, "तुम पाखंडी हो। तुम अच्छे होने का दिखावा करते हो, पर अच्छे हो नहीं। बहुत पहले यशायाह ने परमेश्वर का संदेश सुनाया था, और उसने तुम्हारे बारे में बिल्कुल सही कहा। उसने लिखा कि परमेश्वर कहते हैं: 'ये लोग कहते हैं कि वे मेरा आदर करते हैं, पर यह बस इनके होंठों की बात है। इनके दिल मुझसे बहुत दूर हैं।

uk.L: А {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав їм: «Добре пророкував Ісая про вас, лицемірів, як написано: “Цей народ шанує {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} устами, а серце їхнє далеко від {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}};
uk.B: Він відповів їм: «Як влучно пророкував Ісая про вас, лицемірів! Бо написано: “Цей народ шанує {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}} устами, а серце їхнє далеко від {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}.
uk.R: Ісус відповів їм: «Ви лицеміри. Ви вдаєте із себе добрих, але ви не такі. Ісая правду сказав про вас, коли давно передавав Божу звістку. Він записав, що сказав Бог: “Ці люди кажуть, що шанують {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}, але це тільки слова на їхніх устах. Їхні серця далеко від {{deity_pronoun:мене|Мене}}.

ja.L: そこでイエスは彼らに言われた。「イザヤは、あなたがた偽善者について見事に預言した。こう書かれているとおりである。『この民は唇でわたしを敬うが、その心はわたしから遠く離れている。
ja.B: イエスはお答えになった。「イザヤは、あなたがた偽善者のことを実に見事に預言したものだ。こう書いてある。『この民は唇ではわたしを敬う。しかし、その心はわたしから遠く離れている。
ja.R: イエスは彼らにお答えになりました。「あなたたちは偽善者だ。正しい人のふりをしているが、そうではない。昔、イザヤが神の言葉を語ったが、それはまさにあなたたちのことだった。イザヤは、神が言われたことをこう書き記した。『この人々は、わたしを敬うと口では言う。しかし、それは唇から出る言葉だけだ。その心はわたしから遠く離れている。

decisions.choice: Isaiah 29:13, in the wording of the ancient Greek translation
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes God's complaint through Isaiah against a people whose worship was only outward. The wording follows the Greek translation of Isaiah closely. The Hebrew of Isaiah 29:13 reads "their fear of me is a command of people, learned by rote"; the Greek, followed here, reads "in vain they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commands of people".

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who play a part, whose outward show does not match the heart
decisions.reason: The word was used for an actor on a stage. The quotation shows the meaning: honor with the lips while the heart is far away. This is the only time Mark uses it.

decisions.choice: prophesied well: spoke God's word truly and to the point
decisions.reason: To prophesy is to speak for God. Isaiah's words fit the people of his own day, and Jesus says they fit these men too.

decisions.choice: lips and heart: God looks for worship that comes from within
decisions.reason: The heart is the center of thought and will. This prepares for 7:21, where evil comes from the heart.

decisions.choice: You pretend to be good, but you are not
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word hypocrite.

decisions.choice: say that they honor me, but it is only words from their lips
decisions.reason: Readable says what honoring with the lips means.

decisions.choice: "những kẻ giả hình" (L); "những kẻ đạo đức giả" (B, R)
alternatives: "những kẻ giả hình" at every level
decisions.reason: "Giả hình" is the familiar church word, kept at Literal; "đạo đức giả" is the everyday modern word for a person whose piety is a show, which is the sense the meaning decision gives.

decisions.choice: Jesus calls the Pharisees and scribes "các người"; in the words of Isaiah God says "Ta"
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to opponents and crowds, kept through the chapter (also 7:8-13 and to the crowd in 7:14). God speaking in Scripture says "Ta", with the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence.

decisions.choice: "위선자들" at every level; Readable adds what it means
decisions.reason: "위선자" is the current Korean word for one whose outward show does not match the heart; "외식하는 자" is the older church expression.

decisions.choice: « » for Jesus's words, “ ” for Isaiah
decisions.reason: The quotation of Isaiah inside Jesus's words takes the inner marks, as in Mark 1:2-3; Jesus's words run on to the end of 7:8. In Isaiah's words God speaks, so "me" and "mí" take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "leur cœur" (L); "son cœur" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek takes up the singular "people" with a plural "their"; Literal keeps the plural, which French allows for a people, and Balanced makes it agree with "ce peuple".

decisions.choice: wananipa heshima kwa midomo ... umekaa mbali nami
alternatives: the familiar wording of the Swahili Union Version
decisions.reason: Drafted from the Greek of Isaiah 29:13 as Mark quotes it, not from a Swahili Bible, whose familiar wording of this verse many readers know by heart. A reviewer should check that the wording reads naturally without echoing a copyrighted version.

decisions.choice: nami (with me), with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: In the quotation God is the speaker, so the joined pronoun "nami" takes the span, as the English "me" does.

decisions.choice: the wording of Isaiah 29:13 as in Matthew 15:8
decisions.reason: The Greek of the quotation is the same as in Matthew 15:8, so Literal and Balanced keep the Portuguese of that verse. Readable follows the fuller explanation of the English Readable here.

decisions.choice: "пророчествовал" (L, B); "передал весть от Бога" (R)
decisions.reason: "Пророк" and its family are the settled terms; Readable says what prophesying is, as in Matthew 15:7. The words of Isaiah follow Matthew 15:8-9, where the Greek is the same.

decisions.choice: "तुम" to the Pharisees and scribes
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to everyone with तुम through the book, opponents included, while they say आप to him, as in Matthew 15:3. The Greek "you" here is plural; the context makes that plain.
The term settled for the book; Readable also explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "見事に" (L, B); "まさにあなたたちのことだった" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means that Isaiah spoke to the point (m3). Literal and Balanced use "見事に" so that the same word can turn to irony in 7:9 ("見事に神の戒めを退けている"), as the Greek repeats it; Readable says plainly that the words fit them. God's words in Isaiah are in the plain style, as quoted Scripture.

source.text: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων·

en.L: and in vain they worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, teaching as doctrines the commands of {{gender:people|men}}.'

en.R: Their worship of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is useless. They teach rules that people made up as if they were God's teaching.'

es.B: En vano {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rinden culto, pues enseñan como doctrina lo que son mandatos humanos”.

fr.L: et c’est en vain qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendent un culte, enseignant comme doctrines des commandements {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}}.”

sw.L: na ni bure wanavyoniabudu, wakifundisha amri za wanadamu kama mafundisho.'

decisions.choice: the end of Isaiah 29:13 in the Greek translation
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Isaiah says that their fear of God is a command of men learned by rote. The Greek translation, which Mark follows, says that their worship is in vain because they teach human commands. The sense is close.

decisions.choice: in vain: to no purpose, empty
decisions.reason: Their worship achieves nothing with God.

decisions.choice: teaching human commands as doctrines: passing off their own rules as God's teaching
decisions.reason: The verb takes two objects: what they teach, human commands, and what they present them as, doctrines.

decisions.choice: people (men as the alternative)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, as against God.

decisions.choice: "loài người", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Loài người" (humankind) already takes in men and women, so the English gender setting has nothing to choose between in Vietnamese. The same holds for "loài người", "người ta" and "con người" through this chapter (7:8, 7:15, 7:18-23).

decisions.choice: "사람들" with no gender span, here and through chapter 7
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" already includes men and women, so the English people/men span has no Korean counterpart (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings (meaning decision m3); the reader setting gives the traditional "los hombres". Balanced and Readable say "humanos" and "la gente", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:d’êtres humains|d’hommes}}
decisions.reason: The word is the one for human beings ("men" in the general sense), so the default is inclusive and the traditional "d’hommes" is the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "humains", already inclusive, with no setting.

decisions.choice: wanadamu, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: "Wanadamu" (human beings) already includes men and women; the only male word, "wanaume", would change the meaning, so the gender setting has nothing to change in this chapter (also 7:8, 7:21).

decisions.choice: "ሰዎች" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "people" and "men" for the Greek's generic word. Amharic "ሰዎች" (and "ሰው" with its generic masculine suffixes in 7:15-23) already means human beings in general, so there is no second wording for a setting to offer.

decisions.choice: "людей" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English has gender spans in this passage (7:7, 7:8, 7:15, 7:18-21), the Russian words are already inclusive: "люди" and "человек" cover women as well as men, and "его" after "человек" follows the grammar of the noun. So the Russian has no span.

decisions.choice: No gender spans in this passage
decisions.reason: Where the English has gender spans in 7:7-21 ("people

decisions.choice: "людських" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts "people|men" under the gender setting; Ukrainian "людський", "людина", "люди" already include men and women, so no setting is needed here or in 7:8-23.

decisions.choice: "人間" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts "people (men)" under the gender setting; "人間" is already inclusive in Japanese and sets human commands against God's (m3), so no span is needed. The same holds for "人間の言い伝え" in 7:8.

decisions.choice: the participle clause "教えとして教えながら" placed before the main verb
alternatives: "むなしくわたしを礼拝している、……教えながら"
decisions.reason: Japanese puts a 〜ながら clause before the verb it goes with; the words are the same as the Greek's.

decisions.choice: leaving: abandoning, letting go
decisions.reason: The verb can mean forgive, but here it means to leave behind or neglect.

decisions.choice: the commandment of God: God's law as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular sums up what God has commanded. Verse 10 gives an example.

decisions.choice: God's command against human tradition: the contrast that runs through 7:8-13
decisions.reason: Jesus does not reject every custom. He rejects tradition that is held in place of God's command.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the verse at "the tradition of men"
alternatives: add: the washing of pitchers and cups, and many other such things you do
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add these words, which repeat 7:4 and 7:13. They are not in the earliest manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a tradition that is merely human
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the contrast with God's command.

decisions.choice: mapokeo (L, B); kanuni (R)
decisions.reason: "Mapokeo" (what is handed down) is the Swahili word for tradition, used in Galatians 1:14 and Colossians 2:8. Readable says "kanuni" (rules), as the English Readable says "rules".

decisions.choice: "戒め" (L, B); "おきて" (R)
decisions.reason: God's commandment is "戒め" at Literal and Balanced and "おきて", in kana, at Readable everywhere in the book (7:8-9, 10:5, 10:19, 12:28-31), so the reader meets one word for it. The "human precepts" of 7:7 are a different word, "定め" (B) and "決まり" (R).

records.literal_gloss: And he was saying to them, Well you set aside the commandment of the God so that the tradition of you you might keep.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them, "Well do you set aside the commandment of God, so that you may keep your tradition.
en.B: He went on, "You are very skillful at setting God's command aside so that you can keep your own tradition!
en.R: Jesus went on, "You are very clever! You find ways to ignore what God commands so that you can keep your own rules.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Các người khéo gạt bỏ điều răn của Đức Chúa Trời, để giữ truyền thống của các người.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 너희의 전통을 지키려고 하나님의 계명을 잘도 저버린다.

es.L: Y les decía: «Bien {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} sin efecto el mandamiento de Dios para guardar {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tradición.

am.L: እንዲህም ይላቸው ነበር፦ «ወጋችሁን ትጠብቁ ዘንድ የእግዚአብሔርን ትእዛዝ በሚገባ ትሽራላችሁ።
am.B: ደግሞም እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «የራሳችሁን ወግ ለመጠበቅ ስትሉ የእግዚአብሔርን ትእዛዝ ወደ ጎን በመተው እንዴት የተካናችሁ ናችሁ!

ru.L: И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} говорил им: «Хорошо вы отменяете заповедь Божью, чтобы соблюсти ваше предание.
ru.B: Он продолжал: «Как ловко вы отставляете Божью заповедь, чтобы соблюдать своё предание!

hi.L: और उन्होंने उनसे कहा, "तुम अपनी परंपरा को मानने के लिए परमेश्वर की आज्ञा को ख़ूब टाल देते हो।
